# A copy of eight `@buildanagent/agent-safety` files

`bytes.ts`, `errors.ts`, `hash.ts`, `outcome.ts`, `pending.ts`, `render.ts`, `signer.ts` and `test-signer.ts` are byte-for-byte copies of the same files in `packages/agent-safety/src/`. They give tool results their write outcomes, the progress check its input hash, signed pauses their signers and pending record, and the testing export its fixed-key test signer. The copies date from when the safety package was private, so the published SDK could not depend on it. The safety package now publishes with the SDK, in the same fixed group, and nothing else keeps the copies here: they stay only until a follow-up switches the SDK to the package. Because the SDK would then depend on the safety package, that switch also moves the safety package ahead of the SDK in `RELEASE_ORDER` (`scripts/ci/release-plan.mjs`), so each release publishes it first. The SDK re-exports the signers, the hash, the pending-record types and `SafetyError` from these copies unchanged, and its testing export re-exports `testSigner()` and `TEST_KEY_ID`.

`test/vendored-safety.test.ts` fails if a copy differs from its source, so edit the safety package and copy the files again. Because the copies are byte-identical, a request the SDK signs verifies with the package's own signer over the same key, and `test/pending.test.ts` checks that the two sign identical payloads.

The copies are separate modules, so each holds its own state. `ephemeralSigner()` keeps one random key per module, and a process that loads both the SDK and the safety package has two ephemeral keys: a pause signed by one's default signer does not verify with the other's. Hosts that need both pass one `hmacSigner()` to each.

Once an alpha of `@buildanagent/agent-safety` is on npm, delete this folder. Import from the package's root export and take `testSigner()` from its `testing` subpath, as the SDK plan's dependency rule says.
